chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered the bathhouse, so the owner of the bathhouse said to him, 'Shall I empty it for you?' He said, 'I have no need for that; the believer is more modest than that.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam's response to the bathhouse attendant reveal about the character of a believer?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on social etiquette, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the Shia concept of *haya* (modesty) as an intrinsic humility rather than a demand for status. The Imam’s refusal to clear the bathhouse demonstrates that a true believer does not seek exclusivity or special treatment, embodying the principle of *tawadu* (humility) in daily interactions. This serves as a practical model for social conduct, emphasizing that spiritual rank should not lead to arrogance or separation from the community.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, form sa’adan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> entered the bathhouse, so the one in charge of the bathhouse said to him, ‘I shall empty it for you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no need for me<sup>asws</sup> with regards to that is hidden from that’.
en.sarwar: 35. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn Ali ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid from his uncle Muhammad ibn ‘Umar from those who narrated to him who has said the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, ‘One who believes in Allah and in the Day of Judgment must not enter a bathhouse without a loincloth.’ One day he entered a bathhouse and applied lime that covered his body. He (the Imam) then dropped the loincloth and one of his slaves said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul and the souls of my parents in service for your cause, you always instruct us about the necessity of loincloth but you have dropped it.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Do you not know that lime has fully covered?”’
